pr_title: Add a service to reload config entries that can easily be called though automations

Many (most?) integrations don't support reload, and will require a restart of Home Assistant to cycle unload+load.
How can we make that visible when the user calls the reload service?

Also, how come this is not handled by the Homekit integration?

> Many (most?) integrations don't support reload, and will require a restart of Home Assistant to cycle unload+load.
> How can we make that visible when the user calls the reload service?

We could throw a better exception?

Should also close this:
https://community.home-assistant.io/t/add-service-integration-reload/231940

> 
> Also, how come this is not handled by the Homekit integration?

HomeKit is expecting tight coupling to the device so it knows to announce a configuration change.  We currently don't have a way to detect this and increment the config version as it would require some arch changes to the way HomeKit is implemented. It is doable, but its lower on the list of HomeKit fixes.  Without a second code owner/reviewer for HomeKit, the changes go really slow and there is currently a backlog of HomeKit PRs.
Converting to draft while I rework the error messages so the user gets a better UX when the config entry cannot be reloaded or doesn't exist

issue_context.title: HomeKit media_player in accessory mode does not update state and sources list
issue_context.body: **The problem** Hello @bdraco! Thanks for your work! There are two problems and it has existed for a long time... Tried to configure via UI and via config - same. 1. Media player in accessory mode does not update its state after being unavailable. I am using androidtv integration and when my tv is turned off in Home Assistant it shows as unavailable. After turning on the TV, the status is updated in Home Assistant, but it still to be unavailable in Homekit until it is restarted. As temporary solution i use universal media player wrapper with custom state, but I think that this needs to be reported. 2. Second problem is same. The sources list is not updated after updating them in Home Assistant. Consequently, if the list of sources was not received at the time the homekit was launched (for example, the TV was turned off at the time of launch), then it will not be received at all, until HK is restarted. **What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?** 2021.2.3 **What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?** _No response_ **What type of installation are you running?** Home Assistant Container **Integration causing the issue** HomeKit **Link to integration documentation on our website** https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homekit/ **Example YAML snippet** ```yaml # Put your YAML below this line homekit: - name: "Sony TV" port: 51828 auto_start: true mode: accessory filter: include_entities: - media_player.sony_tv entity_config: media_player.sony_tv: name: "Телевизор" feature_list: - feature: on_off - feature: play_pause - feature: play_stop - feature: toggle_mute - name: "PS4" port: 51829 auto_start: true mode: accessory filter: include_entities: - media_player.playstation_4 entity_config: media_player.playstation_4: name: "PS4" feature_list: - feature: on_off - feature: play_pause - feature: play_stop - name: "Xiaomi Projector" port: 51830 auto_start: true mode: accessory filter: include_entities: - media_player.xiaomi_projector entity_config: media_player.xiaomi_projector: name: "Проектор" feature_list: - feature: on_off - feature: play_pause - feature: play_stop - feature: toggle_mute ``` **Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?** ```txt # Put your logs below this line ``` Current state: Shows in HomeKit: After HomeKit reloaded:

We could update the characteristics when the inputs change, but isn't a way to tell HomeKit controllers (iPhones) that it has changed short of a restart.

Your best bet is to create an automation to reload the homekit config entry (POST to `/api/config/config_entries/entry/<ENTRY_ID>/reload` with a 0 byte body) when the inputs change or the device turns on as that would force all devices to reconnect

`Your best bet is to create an automation to reload the homekit config entry (POST to /api/config/config_entries/entry/<ENTRY_ID>/reload with a 0 byte body) when the inputs change or the device turns on as that would force all devices to reconnect`

@wasp100 use **RESTful Command** (https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/rest_command/): ```yaml rest_command: homekit_reload_sony_tv: url: 'https://YOUR_HA_URL:8123/api/config/config_entries/entry/INTEGRATION_ID/reload' method: post content_type: "application/json" headers: authorization: "Bearer API_TOKEN" ``` Simple way to get **INTEGRATION_ID** of your HomeKit Bridge is: right click on integration card in Settings -> Integration and click **Inspect Element**. Also you can find IDs of your bridges in `/ha_config/.storage/` directory. Don't forget about **API_TOKEN** in request. It can be created in the profile section. Then you can create automation: ```yaml - id: 'ID' alias: Sony TV [HK Reload] description: '' trigger: - platform: state entity_id: media_player.sony_tv attribute: source_list - platform: state entity_id: media_player.sony_tv from: 'off' condition: [] action: - service: rest_command.homekit_reload_sony_tv data: {} ```
We could probably add a service so you don't need the token maybe: `homeassistant.reload_config_entry`

After several days of testing, I conclude that reloading the integration when changing the source list is not the best option (at least with the androidtv integration). Sometimes the current source was not displayed until the homekit panel/app on the iPhone or MacBook was reopened. Probably the integration failed to get the correct list of sources, or the integration simply did not have time to reboot, or HK doesn't update sources immediately when panel displayed in first time after reload.

Perhaps androidtv or homekit integration just need save latest list of sources in memory even TV turned off? Think about it :)

Anyway i found another workaround: define source list on media_player in customize.yaml 
eg:

```yaml
media_player.sony_tv:
  device_class: tv
  source_list:
  - Android TV Launcher
  - External Input
  - YouTube
  - TiviMate
  - Spotify
  - Netflix
  - Vimu Player
  - HDVideoBox
  - TorrServe
  - Twitch App
  - SPB TV
  - Google Cast
```

Everything works well now.
do we have an update on this? would be valued by many .;-)

Currently it works correctly only with trick of define source list in customize.yaml and universal media player wrapper.

@bdraco In addition, 2 more bugs were found in HK Media Player:
1. If media player go into standby state (in [androidtv](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/androidtv/) integration it happen when start screensaver), the homekit displays it as off...

Again hacky solution is crazy:
```yaml
- platform: universal
  name: "Xiaomi Projector"
  device_class: tv
  children:
    - media_player.xiaomi_projector_cast
    - media_player.xiaomi_projector_adb
  state_template: >
    {% if not is_state('media_player.xiaomi_projector_cast', 'off') and not is_state('media_player.xiaomi_projector_cast', 'unavailable') and not is_state('media_player.xiaomi_projector_cast', 'unknown') %}
        {{ states('media_player.xiaomi_projector_cast') }}
    {% else %}
        {% if not is_state('media_player.xiaomi_projector_adb', 'unavailable') %}
            {% if is_state('media_player.xiaomi_projector_adb', 'standby') %}
                idle
            {% else %}
                {{ states('media_player.xiaomi_projector_adb') }}
            {% endif %}
        {% else %}
            off
        {% endif %}
    {% endif %}
```
